current.text: Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry. Applications may allow the user to temporarily view the entire masked password, or the last typed character of the password.

master.text: Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry. Applications may allow the user to temporarily view the entire masked password, or the last typed character of the password.

predecessors.text: Verify that the user can choose to either temporarily view the entire masked password, or temporarily view the last typed character of the password on platforms that do not have this as built-in functionality.

summaries.body: The mapping records V6.2.6 as MODIFIED, MOVED FROM v4.0.3-2.1.12. The predecessor required that the user be able to temporarily view the entire masked password or the last typed character on platforms without that as built-in functionality. On 26 February 2019 vanderaj resolved #570 against V2.1.12 (7501f74d). Mapping and that predecessor — not 4.0 cryptography commits labelled V6.2.6 — are the origin of the password-masking control.

tghosth's 14 July 2020 commit on V2.1.12 replaced "native" with "built-in" in the platform caveat. 5.0 adds a requirement that password fields use type=password to mask entry, and makes reveal behaviour optional ("may allow") rather than something the user must be able to choose. The "platforms that do not have this as built-in functionality" qualifier dropped out.

vanderaj's Resolve #537 on a V6.2.6 slot is the 4.0 Cryptography chapter; Jim's 13 July 2020 revert on V2.1.12 is git noise around that predecessor, not a 5.0 policy change.
